test_title: PYST 18: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 16 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Ribosomes?

Statement A: Ribosomes have no membrane.

Statement B: Digestive hydrolytic enzymes are present in Ribosomes.

Statement C: These are called suicidal bags.

Statement D: Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis.

options.text: Only statements A, B and C

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements A and D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ribosomes have no membrane**: Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins and do not have a surrounding membrane. They are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis**: They facilitate the linking of amino acids to form polypeptides, following the instructions encoded in messenger RNA (mRNA).
 
• Ribosomes can be found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming rough ER.
 
• There are two main types of ribosomes: 70S (found in prokaryotes) and 80S (found in eukaryotes).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digestive hydrolytic enzymes**: These enzymes are found in lysosomes, not ribosomes. Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes for breaking down cellular waste and macromolecules.
 
• **Suicidal bags**: Lysosomes are often referred to as "suicidal bags" because they can digest the cell's own components when they rupture.
 
• **Messenger RNA (mRNA)**: This type of RNA carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosome, where it is translated into a specific protein sequence.
 
• **Transfer RNA (tRNA)**: tRNA is responsible for bringing the correct amino acids to the ribosome during protein synthesis, matching the codons in the mRNA.
 
• **Ribosomal RNA (rRNA)**: This RNA forms the core of the ribosome's structure and catalyzes protein synthesis.
